memory_update.text: New Hotspots should be treated as a rotating chokepoint-discovery funnel rather than a single-sector theme; demand shocks, policy shifts, and supply-chain concentration are the primary organizing variables.
Indium phosphide substrates are a priority underfollowed node for AI optical interconnect research because supply appears concentrated and potentially constrained by China-linked licensing.
Tungsten is a priority defense-material hotspot due to reported China supply dominance, export controls, and war-driven munitions replenishment demand.
Sulphur and sulphuric acid should be tracked as an upstream feedstock chokepoint for copper SX-EW, Indonesian nickel HPAL, fertilizers, and industrial chemicals.
HBM and advanced-packaging sub-suppliers remain a valid second-order discovery lane, but later layers must prove that the market has not already priced the exposure.

Layer 1B should build a candidate universe across US, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Europe, Canada, Australia, and China, with market cap, analyst coverage, segment exposure, and primary-source evidence fields.

layer1a.summary: Layer 1A decomposes 'New Hotspots' into emerging chokepoint themes where breaking news, policy shifts, supply shocks, or underfollowed supplier dependencies may create second-order beneficiaries. The strongest initial lanes are: critical minerals tied to defense replenishment, compound semiconductor substrates for AI networking and optical links, sulphur/sulphuric-acid feedstock disruptions cascading into copper/nickel/fertilizer, one-layer-below HBM and advanced-packaging suppliers, and power/grid infrastructure for AI data centers. This is not a stock recommendation layer; it is a theme map for later evidence collection, candidate universe expansion, and falsification.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: If AI data-center bandwidth demand keeps shifting toward higher-speed optical modules, concentrated indium phosphide substrate supply and China-linked export licensing could become a chokepoint for optical component makers.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Prefer small/mid-cap substrate and optical-component suppliers where InP is material to revenue. Treat large diversified industrials as reference unless segment disclosure is unusually clear.
supply_chain_nodes.node: Indium phosphide substrates and wafers for AI optical interconnects
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Map AXT, Sumitomo Electric, JX Advanced Metals, Coherent, Lumentum, optical component vendors, substrate makers, and downstream transceiver customers. Later layers should verify actual InP revenue exposure, customer mix, backlog, license delays, and capacity expansion timelines.

supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: This is one or two layers below AI accelerators and networking switches; the investable exposure may be hidden in specialty materials, photonics components, and substrate suppliers rather than headline AI chip names.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: AI networking and high-speed optical links may require compound semiconductor substrates that sit several layers below the obvious accelerator and switch vendors.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: Defense demand plus China export controls may sustain tight tungsten supply, benefiting non-China mining, recycling, refining, and hardmetal suppliers if they can qualify material for defense and industrial customers.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Look for USD 300M-10B miners/processors and micro-cap exceptions only if clearly labeled speculative, funded, and permitted. Avoid treating exploration-stage resources as equivalent to qualified supply.

supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Screen for listed tungsten miners, processors, recyclers, hardmetal producers, defense-material suppliers, and companies with tungsten byproduct exposure. Verify ore grade, processing capacity, customer qualification, geopolitical risk, and whether revenue is meaningful.

supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: Tungsten sits outside the usual AI/rare-earth spotlight but may be directly linked to war-driven replenishment and national-security procurement.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: Tungsten is used in armor-piercing ammunition and industrial tools, so simultaneous defense replenishment and export controls can create a materials chokepoint outside the most watched rare-earth narratives.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: Export bans, shipping disruptions, and regional deficits may turn acid availability and logistics into a hidden constraint on copper SX-EW and Indonesian nickel HPAL output.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Search across industrial chemicals, fertilizer, metals processing, shipping, and terminals. The best candidates may have messy classifications and may not screen as copper or battery-metal companies.
supply_chain_nodes.node: Sulphur and sulphuric acid feedstock for copper SX-EW and nickel HPAL
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Map acid producers, smelters with acid byproduct streams, sulphur logistics operators, storage terminals, sulfur burners, fertilizer producers, copper SX-EW miners, and Indonesian HPAL-linked companies. Verify whether companies are net acid sellers, buyers, or exposed to cost inflation.

supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: The headline trade is usually copper or nickel, but the more obscure pressure point may be acid supply, shipping corridors, smelter byproduct output, and regional storage.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: Sulphuric acid is a critical process input for copper and nickel supply chains; shortages can transmit into energy-transition metals, fertilizer, and industrial chemicals.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: As HBM and advanced packaging capacity expands, the most mispriced beneficiaries may be narrower suppliers with scarce know-how, long qualification cycles, and high revenue sensitivity to HBM capex or unit growth.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Favor USD 300M-30B suppliers with disclosed HBM or advanced-packaging exposure. Include larger names only as comparables or if exposure is unusually pure.
supply_chain_nodes.node: HBM and advanced-packaging sub-suppliers below memory producers
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Search for probe cards, burn-in/test sockets, thermal compression bonding, underfill, substrates, TSV-related tools, advanced inspection/metrology, dicing, bonding materials, and thermal interface suppliers. Verify customer qualification and HBM-specific revenue rather than generic semiconductor exposure.

supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: The market may have priced the obvious HBM producers, but not all second-order suppliers are equally followed, especially non-US, sub-USD-50B names with limited English coverage.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: HBM shortages are widely recognized, but bottlenecks may persist in materials, inspection, test, substrates, bonding, and packaging equipment one layer below Samsung, SK hynix, Micron, and foundry leaders.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: Power infrastructure shortages may shift value from hyperscalers and server suppliers toward grid equipment and services companies with backlog, scarce manufacturing capacity, or local permitting advantages.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Prefer small/mid-cap companies with order backlog, capacity additions, and data-center or utility interconnection exposure. Avoid assuming all electrical-equipment companies benefit equally.
supply_chain_nodes.node: AI data-center grid interconnection, transformers, switchgear, and transmission services
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Use Vertiv, Eaton, GE Vernova, Quanta Services, and utilities as reference leaders, then search smaller suppliers of transformers, bushings, switchgear, relays, protection equipment, cables, substations, and EPC subcontractors.

supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: The obvious AI infrastructure names are well covered; smaller electrical suppliers and regional grid contractors may be hidden because they are classified as industrials or utilities rather than AI beneficiaries.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: AI data-center demand translates into power availability, interconnection queues, transformers, switchgear, grid construction, and utility coordination, which can gate deployment even when chips are available.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: If high-density AI racks outgrow conventional air-cooling capacity, qualified liquid-cooling components and integration know-how could become a bottleneck, especially where customers require reliability, leak prevention, and global service.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Focus on USD 300M-10B component suppliers with industrial-fluid, precision-cooling, or electronics-thermal exposure. Treat micro-cap cooling claims as speculative until customer wins are documented.
supply_chain_nodes.node: Liquid cooling and thermal-management components for high-density AI racks
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Map Vertiv and large thermal players as references, then screen for niche pump, valve, connector, thermal interface, heat-exchanger, fluid, and CDU suppliers. Verify data-center revenue rather than general HVAC exposure.

supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: The market often recognizes data-center cooling at the system level, but obscure component suppliers may have higher incremental sensitivity if they are qualified into next-generation rack designs.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: Higher AI rack density increases heat-removal requirements and may drive demand for cold plates, pumps, manifolds, CDU systems, heat exchangers, immersion fluids, sensors, and facility retrofits.

demand_drivers: AI data-center buildout increasing demand for accelerators, HBM, optical interconnects, advanced packaging, power delivery, and cooling infrastructure.
Defense replenishment and munitions demand increasing attention on obscure critical metals such as tungsten.
Policy and export-control shocks affecting China-linked critical materials, including tungsten, sulphuric acid, and indium phosphide supply chains.
Electrification and AI-load growth pressuring grid interconnection, transformers, switchgear, turbines, transmission construction, and backup power.
Battery-material and energy-transition supply chains exposed to sulphur/sulphuric-acid feedstock shocks, especially copper SX-EW and Indonesian nickel HPAL.
Hyperscaler capital spending creating second-order demand for niche suppliers that are one or two steps below obvious leaders.

theme_map.public_market_search_strategy: Start with the broad hotspot, then split into demand shock, scarce input, processing/refining, equipment/capacity, customer qualification, public-market exposure, and falsification. Use mega-cap reference leaders only to identify demand, then deliberately search one or two layers upstream or adjacent for smaller public companies with narrow exposure, low analyst coverage, messy sector classifications, or hidden customer concentration. Prioritize companies where later layers can verify revenue linkage through filings, backlog, customer disclosures, capacity expansions, permits, trade data, or segment margin changes.
supply_side_constraints: Export controls and licensing delays for China-linked strategic materials.
High supplier concentration in niche substrate and materials markets.
Long customer qualification cycles for semiconductor substrates, HBM packaging materials, optics, grid equipment, nuclear components, and defense materials.
Limited spare capacity in specialty refining, wafer fabrication, acid supply, transformers, switchgear, and skilled EPC labor.
Geographic concentration of supply in China, Japan, the Middle East, and a small set of established industrial suppliers.
Feedstock substitution limits where downstream plants cannot easily switch inputs without output disruption.
